findings.title: Missing browser security headers
findings.description: Authentication pages lack hardening headers, weakening defense-in-depth against token theft and UI-redress attacks.
findings.remediation: Add the missing headers at the web server or edge.

findings.title: Session cookie 'sessionid' missing flags
findings.description: Session cookies lacking Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite increase risk of session hijacking and post-MFA token theft.
findings.remediation: Set Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax (or Strict) on all authentication session cookies.

findings.title: Short session token 'sessionid'
findings.description: Session token is under 16 characters, far below the 128-bit NIST minimum. Such tokens are predictable and trivially brute-forceable.
findings.remediation: Generate session identifiers with a CSPRNG providing at least 128 bits of entropy (e.g., secrets.token_urlsafe(32)).

findings.title: No observable rate limiting on authentication endpoint
findings.description: The authentication endpoint did not throttle a burst of requests, making the system susceptible to MFA fatigue (prompt bombing) and OTP brute-force attacks.
findings.evidence: 12 rapid requests to http://127.0.0.1:8080/login; statuses={200: 12}; elapsed=0.07s
findings.remediation: Implement per-account and per-IP rate limits on all MFA challenge endpoints (e.g., 3–5 attempts/min), enable number matching, and lock the account after repeated denials.

findings.title: Weak fallback MFA method offered
findings.description: The authentication flow advertises weak fallback factors (SMS, email OTP). These can be downgraded to by an attacker to bypass stronger factors such as FIDO2/WebAuthn.
findings.evidence: Fallback indicators found: SMS, email OTP
findings.remediation: Prefer phishing-resistant factors (FIDO2/WebAuthn). If SMS/voice must remain, restrict to recovery only and apply additional verification and monitoring.

findings.title: No phishing-resistant MFA factor detected
findings.description: The target does not advertise FIDO2/WebAuthn support. Users rely on OTP or push, which are vulnerable to AiTM phishing and real-time relay attacks.
findings.evidence: No WebAuthn/FIDO2/passkey indicators in login page
findings.remediation: Roll out FIDO2 security keys or platform passkeys and require them for privileged accounts (NIST AAL3).
